title: The trip of a single shot
instruction: Put in order what happens from pressing the button to the hit on the screen.
steps: The phone wraps the action in a packet with the server’s address
Routers pass the packet on, all the way to the server
The server works out whom you hit
The response travels back to all the players
debrief: Every shot in an online game travels there and back through routers. The longer the trip, the higher the ping and the later you see the hit.
why: Everything starts with input from the player.
To travel over the network, the action has to be in a packet with an address.
The packet travels through several routers; each one sends it a bit closer.
The server decides about the hit, not your phone. Otherwise you could cheat.
Everyone who is playing has to know the result.
Only now do you see the hit. The whole trip takes as long as your ping.
